regime_context: Hong Kong thematic leadership is extremely narrow (4 of 17 themes eligible; rotation breadth 0.24) and dominated by Banks (H + HK), which is crowded (z 1.02) and mean-reverting (Hurst tag) — i.e., the leader is not trending cleanly. The absolute-trend gate has historically helped drawdown control here (gate_helps true), so eligible themes get the discipline's benefit; only Banks, Energy (H-shares), High-Dividend Blue Chips, and Conglomerates & Exchange pass it today. No scorable ETF proxy exists for the top themes, so all leans below are expressed on unscorable subjects and carry inherently lower conviction.
emerging_watch: Watch whether Energy (H-shares) overtakes Banks (H + HK) in rank while keeping its 'trend' Hurst tag and a breadth above 0.60 — that confirmed handoff would retire the watch and shift the leadership read away from the crowded mean-reverting leader.

theses.subject: Energy (H-shares)
theses.thesis: Energy is the highest-ranked theme with a trend tag, non-crowded positioning, and passing the absolute-trend gate — i.e., among eligible themes it has the cleanest trend-health profile. Its score is only slightly below Banks but without the crowding flag and without mean-revert texture, making it the most defensible carrier of the trend discipline in a market where the leader is reflexivity-prone.

theses.subject: Banks (H + HK)
theses.thesis: Banks is the leader, but the detector flags it as crowded (z 1.02) and mean-reverting (Hurst tag) — a combination that counsels caution rather than participation. theses.dissent: Banks has the strongest momentum and highest breadth of any theme; if the rotation continues absorbing capital, avoiding strength is exactly the reflexivity failure mode the guardrails warn against — a crowded theme can stay crowded.
